name: Damped high-pass harmonic filter
summary: A shunt filter with a resistor across its reactor, giving low impedance over a broad band of higher harmonics.
description: A damped high-pass filter adds a resistor in parallel with the reactor of a capacitor-reactor branch. Above its corner frequency the filter impedance stays low across a wide band, so it absorbs higher-order harmonics and damps resonances rather than sinking one specific order. The C-type variant adds a second capacitor to remove fundamental-frequency losses in the resistor.

Drawings show the capacitor in series with a reactor that has a resistor in parallel, sometimes with the extra capacitor of the C-type arrangement in series with the reactor. It is used beside tuned filters in static var compensators, large rectifier plants and some converter connection points.

The resistor dissipates real power, so its thermal rating is as important as the electrical values. The symbol does not show the corner frequency or the loss figure, which come from the filter design report.
readingNotes: A resistor across the reactor marks a damped filter.
An extra series capacitor indicates a C-type arrangement.
drawingChecklist: State corner frequency, Mvar and resistor rating.
distinction: A damped high-pass filter covers a band of harmonics; a single-tuned filter sinks one order and has no resistor branch.
